articles.title: Malkovich cancels Israel performance over fabricated quote
articles.description: John Malkovich has canceled a planned performance in Israel after promoters circulated a false quote attributed to him. The American actor was set to perform “The Music Critic” in Tel Aviv in April. A press release quoted him as expressing “solidarity” with the Israeli people, but Malkovich told Hollywood Reporter he never made those statements. The show's Israeli producer acknowledged the mistake, citing “human error," and issued an apology. Israel has faced mounting cultural isolation over the war in Gaza. Malkovich has performed in Israel before, stating that performing in a country doesn’t mean he supports its politics.

articles.title: Syrian Arab Republic — Emergency Mobility Tracking and Cross Border Monitoring Situation Update — Round 21 (07 September 2026)
articles.description: Countries: Syrian Arab Republic, Lebanon Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. OVERVIEW Following the ceasefire in Lebanon announced on 17 April 2026, cross-border movements from Lebanon into the Syrian Arab Republic (hereafter referred to as Syria) have continually declined. Observed cross-border mobility is increasingly characterised by more gradual and stabilised patterns. From 02 March to 07 September, DTM identified 127,788 arrivals across 1,177 communities in all 14 governorates in Syria. Syrian nationals accounted for the overwhelming majority of arrivals, with Lebanese nationals representing less than 1 per cent. Flow monitoring at four assessed Syrian-Lebanese border crossings recorded 761,319 movements into Syria over the same period, of which approximately 98 per cent were Syrian nationals and 2 per cent Lebanese nationals. In addition, 3,870 Lebanese nationals were recorded transiting through Syria towards Jordan, highlighting the continued use of Syria as a route for onward regional movement. The Arida border crossing remains closed following the temporary closure from 6 August due to technical works on the Lebanese side. Consequently, Arida movement figures are available only up to 5 August. Key informants (KIs) cited persistent access constraints for travellers, with those previously using Arida having to rely on alternative crossings located further from Tartous Governorate, increasing travel times and associated costs. The situation remains fluid, and DTM continues to monitor development

articles.description: Countries: Pakistan, Afghanistan Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. Highlights Cumulatively, from 15 September 2023 to 15 August 2026, 2,682,993 individuals have returned. • During the reporting period, the number of returns (-43%) and deportations (-41%) decreased significantly compared to the previous reporting period (16–31 July 2026). The decrease in returns and deportations is likely linked to reduced arrest and enforcement operations during this reporting period. • Since 1 April 2025, 1,828,960 Afghan nationals returned, of which 227,667 (12%) were deported. • Fear of arrest (96%) remained the most important reason among respondents to return to Afghanistan.

articles.title: Cuba’s crises weigh heavily on island’s psyche
articles.description: The psychological toll of daily life in Cuba is pushing many to their breaking point on the Caribbean island of nearly 10 million people. There's no relief in sight as a U.S. energy embargo persists and economic and financial troubles deepen. People are dealing with sweltering nights, water and power shortages, dwindling fuel and crumbling homes, limited public transportation and weak cellphone signals. Cuba’s crises worsened after U.S. President Donald Trump announced in late January that he would impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to the island. Small protests have erupted despite the fear of being detained as anger and frustration boil over.

articles.title: Hormuz impasse deepens: Iran retaliates against US targets after its oil tankers destroyed
articles.description: Iran launched fresh attacks against US targets in the Middle East on Wednesday in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers, dragging the foes deeper into war. Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they attacked 20 US vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for the world's oil and gas that Iran has largely controlled since the war erupted. The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.
